# rebar-debug must trace and record the defect's originating ticket before it closes a bug

## Problem

The `rebar-debug` skill drives a bug to a proven, cited root cause, then throws
away the provenance. Phase 1 ends with the mechanism, Phase 2 fixes it, and the
ticket closes without naming the ticket whose work introduced the defect. Defect
escape rate cannot be measured when escaped defects are not mapped to an origin.

rebar already has the machinery, so this is a skill gap, not a code gap:
`caused_by` is a first-class relation (`graph/_links.py:CANONICAL_RELATIONS`);
`rebar transition <bug> ... closed` accepts `--caused-by=<id>`
(`_commands/transition.py:65,163`); the links feed the `bug_caused_by_fan_in`
metric (`metrics/bug_trends.py:255`) and the deterministic epic-close
`caused_by` floor (`docs/plan-review-gate.md:1091`).

Absent an explicit `--caused-by`, a bug close silently falls back to blame
auto-derivation (`metrics/blame.py:184-227`): it blames `<fixing-commit>~1`
across every path in the ticket's `file_impact` and takes a strict majority of
**all lines in those files**. Two systematic failure modes follow. It attributes
to whoever wrote most of the file rather than whoever wrote the defect. And
because it only ever looks at the paths the *fix* touched, it cannot see the
common case where the fix site is not the cause site — a producer change
introduces an obligation (new field, changed invariant, renamed API) and a
consumer is never updated, so the fix lands in consumer code whose lines may be
years old and correct-at-the-time. There, blame reliably charges the defect to
the consumer's old ticket instead of to the change that shipped the obligation
without updating its consumers, which is exactly the escape worth counting.

The skill has strictly better evidence than that fallback and must supply it.

## Plan

Amend `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` only. No code, no behavior
change, no other file.

1. Add a required attribution step to Phase 1's exit gate (Stage 3), immediately
   before the RCA writeback: find the introducing change by blaming the exact
   lines the confirmed experiment implicated, walk through carrier commits
   (reformat/rename/move), recover the ticket from that commit's
   `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject, and record it.
2. Add an explicit "the fix site is not the cause site" sub-step covering unmet
   obligations and missed consumer updates, with the date test as a cheap
   detector (implicated lines predating the good-to-bad transition cannot have
   caused it) and producer-side search (`git log -S<symbol>`) as the recovery.
3. Route recording through the native surface: `--caused-by=<id>` paired with
   the required `--class` on the bug close, or `rebar link <bug> <origin>
   caused_by` when the link is wanted at the Phase 1 exit instead.
4. Require attribution to meet the root cause's evidentiary standard and
   inherit the fallback's fail-closed discipline, and enumerate four
   resolutions: regression, unmet obligation, omission (attributed by
   scope-of-work), and unattributable (record the searches, leave the link
   unset).
5. Scope attribution to the `defect` and `incomplete-implementation` paths; the
   not-a-bug classifications have no defect to attribute.
6. Gate the bug close on it in "Reporting back" and add a **Defect origin** line
   to the report-back list.
7. Wire the supporting hooks: add the link to the approval-gate own-tracker
   carve-out so recording it needs no user approval; note attribution retention
   on the fast path; point Stage 1's git-history bullet at the exit-gate step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SKILL.md` contains an attribution step in Phase 1 Stage 3 that requires
      identifying the originating ticket before the RCA writeback. Verified by
      `grep -n 'Attribute the defect to its originating ticket' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [ ] The step gives the literal close syntax including `--caused-by`. Verified
      by `grep -c -- '--caused-by=<origin-id>' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning at least 1.
- [ ] The fix-site-is-not-cause-site case is covered as its own numbered
      sub-step. Verified by
      `grep -n 'The fix site is not the cause site' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [ ] The unattributable path is present and fails open to a recorded negative
      result rather than a guess. Verified by
      `grep -n 'Unattributable' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning at least one hit in the attribution section.
- [ ] The bug close is gated on attribution in "Reporting back". Verified by
      `grep -n 'Do not close the bug ticket until its origin is recorded' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [ ] The own-tracker approval carve-out lists the `caused_by` link, so
      recording it is pre-approved. Verified by reading the carve-out paragraph
      and confirming the link appears in its enumerated writebacks.
- [ ] The skill frontmatter gate still passes. Verified by
      `python3 scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] No source file changed. Verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main`
      listing only `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`.

## Testing

This change is documentation-only (one Markdown skill file); it ships no Python
and therefore adds no unit test. It is proven by the repository's own gates plus
the per-criterion greps above:

```sh
python3 scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py
git diff --name-only origin/main
awk 'length>100 {print FILENAME":"FNR}' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md
make lint
```

Expected: frontmatter gate PASSes; the diff lists only
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`; the line-length scan reports no
lines over 100 characters that are not already present on `origin/main`
(pre-existing lines 46 and 488); `make lint` clean.
